fix_gate: Any fix must keep 5/5 byte-identical greedy parity and cut GB10 f16 first-request time to <= 2x the f32 first request.

result: H-SF3 FALSIFIED: GB10 one-shot f16 p1 CLI run prefill 2230 ms; nsys api sum top = cuModuleLoadData 1.35 s, cuLibraryLoadData 0.50 s, HtoD 0.44 s; cuMemGetInfo not in top 8. The 44.8 s is serve-specific.

method: 4 fresh apr serve starts interleaved f32,f16,f32,f16 under flock; p1 (845 tok) twice per server, max_tokens=1, client wall ms
result: H-SF5 HOLDS (the falsifier needed >3x in both pairs; got 2.9x and 1.4x). The real f16 first-use cost on GB10 is +1-3 s, and every later request is 2.5x faster. The M4 44.8 s warmup was a one-off outlier; it ran straight after the shadow lane :8091 released the GPU.
verdict: Flipping the default to f16 is safe on GB10. The fix_gate (<=2x f32 first request) is borderline (1.4x / 2.9x); optional polish is to pre-fill the fp16 cache at model load. Not a 0.70 blocker.
